sec.title: Introduction
sec.p: This document presents terms and definitions for concepts relevant to the Metaverse.
Specifically, the terminology presented in this document:

list-item.p: serve as a sound basis in the understanding of Metaverse;
guide new developments in the field by underpinning mutual understanding; and
serve as a quick and handy reference for those newly introduced to this field.

sec.title: Scope
sec.p: This document provides a concept system and a standard set of terminology related to the Metaverse, from basic concepts to those of the Metaverse ecosystem.
The scope of the vocabulary provided in this document corresponds to that of ISO/IEC JSEG 15.

sec.title: Terms and definitions
sec.p: For the purposes of this document, the following terms and definitions apply.
ISO and IEC maintain terminology databases for use in standardization at the following addresses:

tbx:langSet.tbx:note: A brain-computer interface may facilitate bi-directional communication between the brain and a computing device.

tbx:langSet.tbx:definition: input or output device that senses or actuates the body’s movements by means of physical contact with the user
dedicated electronic device designed to play video games
infrastructure of interconnected entities, people, systems and information resources, together with services which process and react to information from the physical world and the virtual world

tbx:langSet.tbx:note: Wearable devices often have a variety of sensing abilities, but limited power capacity constraining communication and data processing abilities. Wearable devices include electronic devices usable by humans, animals, and other organisms.

tbx:langSet.tbx:note: Photogrammetric measurement is often used for mapping, but also has some engineering applications.

tbx:langSet.tbx:example: End users, operators, acquirers, owners, suppliers, architects, developers, builders, maintainers, regulators, taxpayers, certifying agencies, and markets.

sec.title: General
sec.p: The definition of a “metaverse” has long been subject of controversy.

sec.title: Approach
sec.p: In order to define any concept, it is necessary to determine the essential characteristics of the concept, where additions or subtractions to these characteristics will no longer define the concept.

sec.title: Background
sec.p: The word “metaverse” originated from the science fiction Snow Crash written by Neal Stephenson in 1992 [34] Reference .

In popular culture, the term “metaverse” is commonly used as a generalized entity beyond the Internet, as a massively multi-player virtual world experienced through immersive technologies with comprehensive sensory integration through human computer interfaces.
The group has considered a few popular definitions of the “metaverse”, including:

list-item.p: From [31] Reference : “universal, immersive virtual world that is facilitated by virtual reality (VR) and augmented reality (AR)”
From [32] Reference : persistent and immersive simulated world that is experienced in the first person by large groups of simultaneous users who share a strong sense of mutual presence
From [33] Reference : an infinite and persistent set of computer-generated virtual worlds that may be accessed via some human computer interface

sec.title: Considerations
sec.p: WS 1 has considered various definitions, common perspectives and expectations on the term “metaverse” and has come to the following conclusions based on consensus.
Essential characteristics of the “metaverse” include:

def.p: as in the items in the experience is virtual
where it is experienced through human-computer interaction
where the experience is spatially organized according to some notion of location
where users can directly interact with it and receive feedback

sec.p: Common characteristics expected by popular culture include:

def.p: where there can be many simultaneous users
between users across virtual world systems
where actions and events in the virtual world persists after a user leaves
where user actions are performed in real-time

sec.title: Consensus
sec.p: The resulting consensus arrived at this definition for “metaverse”:

disp-quote.p: metaverse: interactive virtual world that incorporates spatial referencing experienced through immersive technologies

sec.p: There are no normative references in this document.
